question: What is the main physical outcome of body scarification?

question: In history, why did many Nigerian communities use facial marks?

options.B: To show ethnic identity and lineage

explanation: Spot on! Traditional facial marks acted like a visual passport to show a person's hometown, family roots, and community heritage. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h1)

question: What tool do traditional practitioners commonly use for scarification?
explanation: Traditional practitioners usually rely on locally crafted metal blades or sharp stones rather than sterile hospital equipment. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason traditional healers make therapeutic cuts on the body?

options.A: To rub local herbal medicine into the body
options.B: To permanently change the person's facial shape
options.C: To remove unwanted body hair follicles
options.D: To test the pain tolerance of young children

explanation: That's right! These cuts help local remedies absorb directly into the skin or tissues for quicker healing according to traditional beliefs. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h2)

question: Which serious infection can easily spread by sharing unsterilized blades during scarification?
explanation: Exactly! Unclean cutting tools transfer blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B and HIV directly from person to person. Safety first! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h3)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fresh scarification cut that is red, swollen, and draining pus. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Normal healing of deep skin tissue
options.C: A healthy immune response to the ink

explanation: Spot on! Pus and swelling are classic signs that bacteria entered the wound due to unsterile tools or dirty substances applied to the cut. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h3)

question: How would you describe a keloid?

options.A: Overgrowth of thick scar tissue beyond the wound
options.B: A pale patch of skin lacking normal pigment
options.C: A temporary bruise caused by blunt trauma
options.D: An open skin ulcer that refuses to heal

explanation: Correct! Keloids happen when the skin produces extra collagen during healing, creating firm, raised scars that spread past the original cut. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h4)

question: Why might someone with noticeable facial scarification face social challenges today?

options.B: They may experience social stigma and discrimination
options.C: They will lose the ability to speak clearly
options.D: Their body will automatically develop chronic malaria

explanation: Spot on. Shifting societal views and modern settings can sometimes lead to unfair judgment against visibly marked individuals, impacting their peace of mind. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when they notice skin scars during a physical exam?

options.A: Immediately report the client to local police

options.C: Inspect the skin calmly and professionally

question: Why must a nurse know the difference between traditional scarification and self-harm scars?

question: Which vaccine is super important to give if a client has a fresh, unsterilized scarification wound?
